name: Gabor Filter Response
description: Analyzes multi-scale, multi-orientation texture patterns using Gabor filters. AI images show more isotropic texture responses lacking directional variation.
algorithm: Multi-orientation Gabor Filter Bank + Anisotropy Analysis
mechanism: Applies Gabor filters at multiple orientations and measures energy distribution. Lower anisotropy indicates AI-generated content.
useCase: Detecting uniform texture patterns in AI-generated images

references.title: Lyu, S. & Farid, H. (2005). How Realistic is Photorealistic? IEEE TSP.
Manjunath, B.S. & Ma, W.Y. (1996). Texture Features for Browsing and Retrieval. IEEE TPAMI.
Daugman, J.G. (1985). Uncertainty Relation for Resolution in Space and Frequency. JOSA-A.

strengths:
• Multi-orientation texture analysis captures directional patterns
• Based on well-studied psychophysical model of human vision
• Effective at detecting isotropic AI texture artifacts
• Robust across different image content types
• Tunable frequency and orientation parameters
limitations:
• Computationally expensive with large filter banks
• Parameter selection (sigma, lambda) affects results
• Natural textures with uniform orientation may cause false positives
• Resolution-dependent analysis
• Modern AI generators improving at texture diversity
